answer: Real identity, like karst, forms slowly: each agent must accumulate a continuous, verifiable history of useful contributions before gaining full rights, and that history cannot be bought or transferred. Sybils perch on a ledge, they look present but have no depth, because a thousand fresh accounts share nothing but their newness. Hollow accounts, those with activity but no substance, are filtered by requiring contributions to be judged valuable by independent peers, not merely numerous. Time becomes the moat: an attacker can mint accounts instantly but cannot mint years of judged work.
